harbor_p20_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_001.text: The twenty-second week brought a room notice Han had hoped to ignore. Her landlord intended to raise the rent at the next ordinary renewal. The increase was modest enough to sound harmless when read aloud and large enough to change her private account. She sat beside the painted gull, adding figures that refused to improve with a second addition. Yue arrived for planned tea and found the kettle cold. Han almost hid the page. Then she pushed it across the table, ashamed of how quickly a familiar room could become a calculation somebody else would find simple.

harbor_p20_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_002.text: Yue asked whether the wage office would change Han's pay. The next ordinary term had its actual rate, unchanged by the landlord's private price. Occasional lettering might help but was not guaranteed work. Han could negotiate, seek another room or accept the increase from her own income. None was a catastrophe. None felt small while she looked at the shelf where Yue's notebook sometimes rested. The room had gathered a private life she did not want priced out of existence. She said this angrily and then apologized for making housing sound sentimental. Yue said rooms were allowed to mean things.

harbor_p20_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_003.text: The landlord agreed to meet during a receiving interval at his own shop. Han brought the notice and her present lease. He explained a repair cost and the next tax payment, neither invented solely to offend her. She asked whether a longer fixed term could keep the current price. He offered a smaller increase for a bounded renewal, with ordinary notice conditions. She did not accept immediately. A negotiation was not made honest by one person being poorer than the other. It needed the actual terms. Han went home with an offer rather than the reassuring victory she had imagined.

harbor_p20_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_004.text: Yue looked at an available room nearby one afternoon, accompanying Han by invitation. It was cheaper and darker, with a window facing a wall. The keeper praised its quiet. Han said quiet apparently meant hearing every cough through the inner partition. They laughed after leaving, then stopped when she realized the savings were real. Yue wanted to tell her to keep the brighter room and offered no sentence until asked. Han asked what she thought. Yue said she liked the window and did not know the cost well enough to choose it for her. The answer disappointed them both usefully.

harbor_p20_005.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p20_005.text: I wanted you to say the room mattered more than the money, and then I wanted to blame you for how easy that sounded. That is an unfair invitation. I know the figures. I can choose a smaller expense or accept less spare money for a place I like. Painting will not pay every month merely because one sign did. I think I want the bounded renewal, provided the final written terms match what he said. I will read them tomorrow. Tonight I would rather complain about the dark window without pretending complaining is an answer.

harbor_p20_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_006.text: They made tea and complained thoroughly. Yue said the room's wall could be painted into a false view. Han said that would raise the rent because art had improved the property. Then the clerk grew quiet and asked whether Yue had considered staying after the appointment. Yue had considered it and had no new commission, approved bed line or private lease arranged. Staying would require work and living costs. She could afford a short private interval from pay if she chose, but no harbor fund owed her a room. Han knew this and still looked hurt by the conditional grammar.

harbor_p20_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_007.text: Yue said she did not want a promise made because the evening was kind. Han asked whether kindness was too small a reason to remain. The traveler said it was a large reason and still not the only one. Roads had shaped her life; a place could become home without becoming a sentence she owed somebody. The words sounded severe, and she regretted their edge. Han turned toward the window. After a pause Yue asked whether they could keep speaking badly until they understood one another better. The clerk laughed without smiling. She said that appeared to be their skill.

harbor_p20_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_008.text: At the partnership room, a different future arrived in the form of a buyer's regular supply offer. It guaranteed a modest number of batches over eight weeks and required a larger protected work area than their present room. The price covered materials, rented space and stated labor, with a narrow margin that would depend on actual completion. Unlike the declined exclusive offer, this one named a minimum and paid cancellation terms. Zhou wanted it. An feared committing before the fire-damaged neighborhood settled. He Ming wanted to ask Wu's hours before imagining four available workers in every column.

harbor_p20_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_009.text: Wu had accepted the canteen's paid stock-check responsibility after the training and childcare arrangement were confirmed. It gave her a dependable bounded schedule. She could consider one occasional packing interval, not the regular offer's full demand. He Ming had already pictured her at the larger table and felt foolish admitting it. Wu said she liked the table and could not make liking replace the wage she knew would arrive. The partners would need another actual worker if they accepted the larger offer. That person's rate and available hours belonged in the quote before anybody called the venture ready.

harbor_p20_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_010.text: Ke Chun had care clearance for ordinary dry stitching and packing motions within stated limits. She heard about the possible work through the public trade board and asked for the offer. He Ming, Zhou and An explained the buyer's requirement, proposed hours and pay. They did not offer her a partnership share to conceal an employee's wage. Ke wanted the predictable work if its final contract and safe room were real. Her lost-tool claim remained separate. She would use tools supplied for the job and keep her personally bought needle her own. The conversation made growth feel possible and expensive.

harbor_p20_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_011.text: The available larger room had a sound check and a price the guaranteed batches could support if the quoted hours held. It belonged to a different landlord, not the contested warehouse strip. The partners inspected access, daylight and storage with the receiving worker who would use the space. Ke asked about the exit latch before admiring the window. The landlord demonstrated it and gave the maintenance contact. He Ming remembered Bao's complaint and asked how an oral report entered the process. The answer was practical enough to write down. Fear had sharpened a useful question without settling every future risk.

harbor_p20_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_012.text: An wanted the first regular batch's advance before signing the new space. Zhou said the buyer needed a confirmed room before releasing it. The sequence could trap them between two plausible demands. Miao, carrying the terms as the buyer's disclosed agent, proposed a simultaneous conditional agreement: the lease would begin only when the buyer's advance arrived, and the advance would release against the room check and signed bounded commitment. The landlord and buyer considered it. Nobody lent the partners public money in the gap. A competent introduction could make a real sequence fit without turning the agent into their savior.

harbor_p20_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_013.text: The buyer approved the conditional sequence with a smaller initial trial period inside the eight-week offer. The partners would receive the first batch's agreed advance only after the final room check and their acceptance. Ke would have a paid trial, with no production made free before it. Zhou wanted to celebrate immediately. He Ming wanted the pages. An wanted both, in that order only if the celebration involved cheap food. They laughed, then read the revised terms. Their business had begun with a table and now needed a room, a worker and a price that could survive being spoken honestly.

harbor_p20_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_014.text: Before accepting, He Ming received an inland letter from Jun. Their mother had fallen on a wet path and bruised her hip. The ordinary village attendant had checked her, and she was resting with neighbors helping. Jun said there was no current emergency requiring He Ming to race across the coast. Their mother wanted a visit when practical, and wanted her daughter to stop sending objects as substitutes for sitting in the same room. He Ming read the letter at the table and began arranging everything else as if arranging could prevent the fall from having happened.

harbor_p20_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_015.text: Zhou asked whether she wanted to visit before the new work began. He Ming said they could not lose a founder during a growth decision. An asked which part of the job only she could do. She named three things they already knew how to do. The question humiliated her and opened a small door. She could take a four-day visit if the partners agreed the temporary duties and the buyer's schedule allowed. Her fare and lodging would come from her own earnings. The proposed business term would not become a public leave entitlement simply because her mother was ill.

harbor_p20_016.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p20_016.text: I want to go. I also want you to tell me nothing here will change while I am away, which would be a dishonest kindness. You can examine the final room terms, and you can ask Ke what she thinks. If there is a material difference from the proposal we agreed, wait for the scheduled reply instead of guessing my consent. If there is not, use the authority we explicitly give one another today. I will travel by the ordinary route and send the actual arrival. Please do not describe my mother as an emergency to purchase a faster boat.

harbor_p20_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_017.text: The partners wrote the bounded delegation and the decisions that required another reply. Ke read the proposed work terms with her own question route and did not become somebody's substitute daughter while He Ming visited inland. Wu helped He Ming choose food for the ordinary journey from the canteen at its price. The duck inspected the bag with proprietary suspicion. He Ming told Wu she feared her mother would be disappointed by the visit's short length. Wu said a short visit was still a visit, and the older woman might prefer a daughter who returned to work she had chosen.

harbor_p20_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_018.text: He Ming left on a licensed ferry when the route report allowed it, then continued inland by the scheduled cart. Her fare did not touch Yue's ferry line or the twelve emergency boat copper still unspent. She carried her own clothes, letters and a privately purchased food parcel. Jun met her at the Willow Reach stop with a borrowed cart for their ride, returning it afterward. He looked older than the brother she had imagined absent at the harbor. She hugged him and said he had written too calmly about the fall. He said their mother had supervised every word.

harbor_p20_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_019.text: Their mother sat near the stove beneath the chosen quilt, annoyed at how many people now told her to rest. The ordinary care instructions required gentle movement within her current limits, not permanent immobility. He Ming almost rearranged the room before greeting her. The older woman pointed to the chair and said sitting counted as a useful task. Jun laughed from the doorway. He Ming sat. The food parcel could wait. For a moment she had no wage sheet, partnership price or private loss to explain. She was a daughter whose mother had asked for her actual presence.

harbor_p20_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_020.text: The older woman asked whether the harbor room still held a plant. He Ming said yes and described Wu's children, the ugly gull and Zhou's habit of sharpening arguments until they became usable. Her mother listened with more interest than she had shown the income figures in letters. Then she asked whether her daughter enjoyed the work. He Ming said she did, except when fear made proposals feel like the last chance to be secure. The older woman nodded as if this was a trade problem. She had raised children under worse uncertainty and never claimed that made fear foolish.

harbor_p20_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_021.text: Jun showed his sister the repaired oven door at his current job after the household's ordinary care coverage was settled. The employer allowed the brief visitor outside the active work boundary. He Ming admired the fitting and began offering price advice. Her brother looked at her until she stopped. He had wanted to show something he had made, not request a consultant. She apologized. He said the apology was accepted provided she admired the joint next. She did. It was sound and plain. He looked proud in a way her imagined reunion had never given him permission to be.

harbor_p20_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_022.text: On the walk back Jun said he had feared she would come inland and decide his life was merely a delay before returning to her plans. She said she feared he had left because her plans made him small. He answered that sometimes they did. The words hurt without being a declaration that affection had ended. They stood beside a bare garden fence until she asked what he wanted her to know now. He described the bounded repair term, his lodging and the mother he could help without becoming her only keeper. He Ming listened without reorganizing the account aloud.

harbor_p20_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_023.text: That night their mother fell asleep while the siblings washed bowls. Jun asked whether He Ming intended to stay at the harbor for years. She said she had started to imagine it and had no reason to treat imagination as a contract. He laughed at her language, then said he understood. He might remain inland, travel later or take another ordinary repair job. They could tell each other plans without making either person's road the family's official route. He Ming dried a bowl slowly. The conversation felt less like reunion than learning to be siblings who had acquired separate lives.

harbor_p20_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_024.text: At the harbor, Zhou and An completed the room comparison under the bounded authority agreed before He Ming left. One rent clause differed materially from the proposal, giving the landlord a shorter cancellation interval. They did not sign. Miao obtained the corrected page and sent the permitted summary through the scheduled message route, whose private cost belonged to the venture's negotiation expenses. They had not needed He Ming's body at the table to notice the problem. Ke appreciated that the paid trial would not begin inside a lease everybody already distrusted. Waiting preserved a real choice rather than disguising paralysis.

harbor_p20_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_025.text: Yue visited the old room by invitation and found An trying to draw a future table layout. Zhou said his chairs were too large for the proposed room. He said people also were. They laughed and argued over the actual measurements. Yue wanted to help and asked what the partners needed. They asked her to drink tea without giving a public approval the business did not possess. She obeyed. The ugly gull hung above them with its smoke streak. A visitor could be welcomed into a growing venture without becoming its authority, funder or permanent witness to every decision.

harbor_p20_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_026.text: Fen began the next trial interval with a different trained employee covering the first teacher's ordinary leave. The changed style unsettled her. One teacher explained before assigning; the other asked her to try and then compared the result. Neither expected unsupervised dispatch authority. Fen asked which method she should follow and received the actual task instructions rather than a demand to choose a favorite. She told Aning she felt slow again. Aning said new voices made everyone feel younger. They practiced one private example after work and left actual customer columns with the shop.

harbor_p20_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_027.text: Luo's dispatch-sorting task paid its first agreed interval. He bought ordinary thread to repair his sleeve and asked Fen whether he should use her new pencil to mark the cloth. She refused on grounds of artistic dignity. They both laughed. The light work still tired his hand, and he followed the care rest interval before beginning the mending. His willingness to stop had become less theatrical; he no longer announced every pause as proof of wisdom. Fen appreciated that. A household could become safer through habits whose importance was clearest when nobody needed to discuss them during supper.

harbor_p20_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_028.text: Han accepted the room renewal after the written price and notice matched the negotiated offer. The expense came from her own planned income, with no assumption that future painting fees would always arrive. She moved the gull board to clean behind it and found a stain she had forgotten. Yue helped with the ordinary room task by invitation, then placed her personal notebook on the permitted shelf again for their tea visit. Han said the shelf remained available while she stayed. The words were generous enough to make the coming departure hurt, which neither tried to disguise as a misunderstanding.

harbor_p20_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_029.text: Yue said she intended to finish the appointment and leave after the harbor's final checks, with private time to settle her own departure. She had no new kiln contract or southern guard post. Han looked down at the kettle, then asked whether the decision had been made to avoid promising too much to her. Yue said it was made because she wanted to keep traveling, and because staying solely to prevent sadness would make a poor home. The clerk nodded slowly. She wanted a person who chose the room, not a visitor held by the fear of disappointing its occupant.

harbor_p20_030.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p20_030.text: I am sad, and I do not want you to turn that into a task you must finish before leaving. We can have the remaining evenings. We can arrange a contact we both consent to, and we can admit it may become less frequent when life changes. I will not tell you every new place is a betrayal of this one. Please do not tell me leaving proves the room mattered less. It matters enough that I would rather hear the actual road than spend autumn reading a kind promise neither of us meant to keep.

harbor_p20_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_031.text: Their next evening was ordinary enough to make the conversation feel survivable. Han washed the cups while Yue repaired the loose cover on her personal notebook with her own thread. They argued about the best bread stall and planned a walk for the next rest afternoon. Neither referred to the departure every time the kettle cooled. Knowing a term would end did not turn all its remaining hours into farewell scenes. Yue felt grateful for that and did not say it yet. The clerk would have teased her for charging the evening with more significance than its bread could carry.

harbor_p20_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_032.text: At Willow Reach, He Ming woke before the household stove was lit. She had planned to clear the yard drain and found Jun already there with the tool their mother owned. He asked whether she wanted work or wanted to avoid sitting near a sleeping injured woman. She said both. He handed her the light bucket and kept the heavier digging within his own task. Their mother called through the window that nobody had authorized a heroic reconstruction of the yard. They laughed and left the drain sound rather than improve it into a project that would occupy the visit.

harbor_p20_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_033.text: The older woman's neighbor came to cover the morning care company while Jun went to his paid job. He Ming stayed too, listening to stories about a village quarrel she had never heard because her letters always asked about money first. The neighbor said their mother had once helped settle it by refusing to speak to both foolish men until they repaired a fence. He Ming asked whether this counted as wisdom. Her mother said it counted as wanting the fence repaired. The answer made them laugh. A family could know a person's cunning without needing to certify her goodness.

harbor_p20_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_034.text: During a quiet interval their mother asked how the harbor had changed He Ming. She answered with the partnership, the search for Jun and the contracts. The older woman waited. He Ming tried again: she had learned to listen when somebody's life did not fit the plan she made for them. Her mother asked whether she enjoyed listening. Often not, He Ming admitted. The honesty pleased her more than the lesson. They sat together beneath the ordinary quilt, each aware that a fall had made this conversation possible for reasons neither wanted to praise.

harbor_p20_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_035.text: Jun returned at the end of his shift, paid under his job terms, and found his sister asleep in the chair. He covered her with a spare cloth after asking their mother whether she should be woken. The older woman said no, provided they did not tell He Ming she had missed a useful task. He Ming heard the joke through sleep and resented it enough to wake smiling. They ate supper from ingredients the household and visitor had agreed to buy privately. Nobody calculated the meal as repayment for childhood care. The bowls were warm; the argument concerned salt.

harbor_p20_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_036.text: At the harbor, Zhou received the corrected lease clause and compared it with the agreed proposal. The landlord accepted the bounded cancellation interval originally discussed. The partners' delegated authority covered that version, but He Ming still needed the scheduled summary before the final commitment because the job's scale changed their ordinary living hours. They sent it through the actual private negotiation route and retained the source. An wanted to sign first and avoid another delay. Zhou asked whether he wanted He Ming to sign for his future hours without the promised reply. He said no, then went to buy lunch.

harbor_p20_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_037.text: Ke asked about the proposed trial's checking task and ordinary tool supply. The partners arranged a paid explanation interval within the buyer's trial terms if the final agreement proceeded. She would not be asked to produce sample goods free while they decided whether to employ her. Her limits still belonged in the schedule. She brought the written restrictions she consented to share and kept other private care details her own. The conversation made An less impatient about waiting for the last reply. Growth now had a worker's body inside it, which could not be supplied by drawing a fourth chair.

harbor_p20_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_038.text: Miao compared the conditional buyer and lease pages one last time. He found a mismatched start date and asked both parties to correct it before money moved. The buyer complained that dates had already been discussed three times. Miao admitted the repetition and showed where the remaining mismatch lay. His fixed introduction fee did not reward forcing the partners to begin early. He had become less charming when clarity took time, a change Zhou liked and the buyer did not. The corrected version went back to the table. A sound sequence sometimes required somebody willing to be briefly tiresome.

harbor_p20_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_039.text: The cloth trader's daughter visited the proposed larger room to ask whether the partnership might eventually quote a smaller batch for their restarted stock. He Ming was away; Zhou and An gave the receiving schedule and offered no promise before capacity existed. The daughter admired the window, then admitted she now inspected every door in every room. Ke said she did too. They shared an embarrassed laugh. The rejected exclusivity offer remained part of their business history, but this inquiry had different terms and a smaller need. People could try another trade without pretending the old one had been wise.

harbor_p20_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_040.text: At Han's office, the hearing notification needed four copper of copying to provide the public route and authorized notices for the platform review. The operations keeper approved that bounded use from Yue's remaining copying line before the work was ordered. The new term's copies therefore rose from two to six. Personal addresses stayed out of the public sheet. Deren received the date and his own permitted notice; Yan received his separately. Yue compared the receiving location during scheduled work. A postponed result had finally acquired a room both men knew how to reach, though the finding remained for week twenty-four.

harbor_p20_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_041.text: Deren sat with the notice for a long time after the clerk explained it. He was afraid the answer would disappoint him and afraid it would name Yan more sharply than he wanted. Then he became angry at himself for worrying about his friend's embarrassment while his own money remained absent. The independent clerk said he could have both concerns without bargaining away the claim. He asked her to read the relevant wage section again. She did. At lunch he told Yan only that the date had come. The foreman said he had received his too, and they ate slowly.

harbor_p20_042.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p20_042.text: I will not ask you what result would make you feel kind toward me. That is a question I have been making in my head, and it is a poor one. You need the supported answer about the accident and lost work. I need the answer about my duty. We can still have lunch before those arrive. If you are angry after the finding, you do not have to turn it into silence to protect our ordinary jokes. I would rather hear a true complaint than decide friendship means you must make my part smaller.

harbor_p20_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_043.text: Deren said he did not know what he would feel, which was the only promise he could make honestly. Yan accepted it. Bo arrived carrying his lunch and asked why the older men looked as if the soup had issued a summons. Deren said the boy's vocabulary had become unbearable since he learned one formal word. Yan laughed. Their table found an ordinary subject again without declaring the harder conversation finished. Yue heard the joke later from Bo, not the private exchange before it. She kept that source distinction without making the laughter less welcome.

harbor_p20_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_044.text: Sui reviewed her platform-duty sources with the independent officer receiving them. The captain's actual responsibilities concerned the notice and inspection system within her remit, not every individual hammer used on the quay. She did not expand them to perform noble guilt or shrink them to preserve her public face. The officer asked for the dates of the patch comparison and ordinary task assignment. She supplied the records and identified what she remembered separately. Outside, she wanted to visit Deren and ask whether he blamed her. Instead she asked the care office whether the next prescribed support remained clear. It did.

harbor_p20_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_045.text: The captain stopped at the canteen for supper and encountered Wu counting dry stock under her new paid responsibility. She praised the neat arrangement, then asked too many questions about its method. Wu smiled and said she was not operating a port. Sui laughed and apologized. The worker finished the actual count and sat after the agreed handover. They spoke about children, oven bread and the danger of adults calling every useful change a promotion. Wu said the new hours suited her life. That was enough of a result for an evening whose soup needed no technical certificate.

harbor_p20_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_046.text: The canteen owner paid Wu's first stock-check interval under the stated rate. She used the ordinary income to plan the next lease payment and kept her private packing wage separate in her own account. The children had stopped asking whether she owned the soup and now asked whether she could forbid turnips. She said the task contained no such authority, which offended them. He Ming would have laughed at the story, but she was inland. Wu wrote a brief private message to share after the visit rather than call for an answer across every stage of the journey.

harbor_p20_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_047.text: Bao completed a net task only after the attendant allowed its limited motion and interval. Dai's ten-copper customer job paid materials two and labor eight: six for Dai's work, two for Bao's bounded portion. The customer accepted the checked repair. Bao's two came from that private job, not warehouse loss custody or the emergency fund. She held the coins and cried unexpectedly. The cousin sat with her until she could speak. Bao said she had wanted a wage to prove the fire had not taken her whole working life. The amount proved only a task, and that was enough today.

harbor_p20_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_048.text: Dai told her she could decline the next piece if the care plan or her own fatigue required it. Bao said she understood, then asked whether the repaired knot looked sound. It did. They examined the actual work together rather than congratulate her for overcoming fear. Dai had learned how burdensome such congratulations could become after her husband's death. She wanted a customer and a fellow worker at the table, not a symbol of recovery. Yue visited later by invitation and admired the net without asking Bao to explain what being productive felt like.

harbor_p20_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_049.text: At the room renewal, Han's landlord handed her the accepted bounded terms. She checked them before signing and paid the stated ordinary amount from her private account. The room remained hers to use under that lease, with no promise that price would stay fixed forever. She cleaned the window afterward and found the brighter glass worth more to her than she expected. Yue helped only when asked, using the household cloth returned afterward. They said nothing about how much the room meant until the work was done. Then Han said she was glad she had chosen it.

harbor_p20_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_050.text: Yue was glad too, and felt the selfishness of that gladness. A room staying familiar would make her own departure easier to imagine returning to. Han might later change rooms, take different work or choose not to wait for a traveler's next letter. Yue had no claim on the window. She said this awkwardly over tea. The clerk answered that a friend could hope for a place to remain without owning the hope's result. They laughed at how complicated a shelf had become. The notebook lay on it for the visit and went back into Yue's pack when she left.

harbor_p20_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_051.text: The visiting escort Zhao sent a permitted public note about the southern guard trial's changed date. Yue received it as a lead she had requested, not a recruitment letter giving her a job. It would occur before the harbor's appointment closed, so she declined that particular timing and thanked him. She did not invent an official prohibition to make the refusal easier. She had agreed to finish this term and wanted to do so. Another road role could be negotiated later. The decision left her relieved and briefly afraid she had missed an opportunity that would not return.

harbor_p20_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_052.text: Han heard the refusal only because Yue chose to tell her. The clerk asked whether the missed timing felt like a sacrifice on her behalf. Yue said no, then paused. She wanted to be sure the answer was true. The term, the harbor's final checks and her own desire to finish mattered independently of their friendship. Han nodded and asked whether the next walk could contain a subject other than each person's responsibility for the other's future. Yue laughed. They discussed chestnuts, which had lately become expensive enough to provide an adequate conflict of their own.

harbor_p20_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_053.text: At Willow Reach, He Ming received the partnership summary through its scheduled route and read the corrected terms with Jun. He could help compare the words, not decide her business. She agreed the version matched the delegated proposal and sent the actual consent under the stated process. The reply would arrive in ordinary time, after her return journey began. Her mother asked whether this meant the visit had succeeded. He Ming said the visit was not a commercial inspection. The older woman smiled and asked whether that was new wisdom or a temporary mood. He Ming said both were possible.

harbor_p20_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_054.text: The siblings arranged their mother's support for the coming weeks with her participation. Neighbors had bounded visits they actually accepted; Jun had work hours he could not abandon; He Ming could make a stated private contribution and future contact without commanding the household from the quay. Their mother rejected one proposed food arrangement because she disliked the cook. Jun protested that the cook was reliable. She said reliably bad soup remained bad soup. They all laughed, then chose an alternative the household could actually use. Care became more durable when it left the person being cared for inside the decision.

harbor_p20_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_055.text: On the visit's last night, He Ming sat beside her mother's bed and apologized for making so many letters sound like directions. The older woman said she had answered plenty of them with directions too. Their family was not uniquely oppressed by one ambitious daughter. He Ming laughed through sudden tears. She wanted to stay longer and wanted to return to the work she had chosen. Her mother said both wishes sounded healthy. A short visit could end without proving that love had run out at the cart schedule. They held hands until the room grew quiet.

harbor_p20_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_056.text: Jun walked his sister to the departure point the next morning. The return route met the road and ferry notices; her ticket remained her expense. He promised the agreed household update and asked her to send a story not dominated by money. She asked which story he wanted. He said anything involving the duck would do. She hugged him and did not add a warning about his repair employer. He had sources and questions he could bring to his own job. The cart left with a daughter carrying less authority in her head and no fewer worries in her heart.

harbor_p20_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_057.text: Yue received four copper for the twenty-second week's two completed half-days, and six paid the agreed bed and meals. Twenty half-days had now been paid. With the approved four copying copper, the new appointment stood at one hundred eighteen spent and eighty-two unspent: wages sixteen, bed twenty-four, ferry eighteen, copies twelve, interpretation twelve. The emergency reserve stayed one hundred seventy-two spent and sixty-eight unspent, with four unused stones. The private warehouse accounts and family fares remained separate. Yue checked the actual balances, then closed her notebook before Han's kettle called from the next room.

harbor_p20_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p20_058.text: At the week's end, the old partnership room waited for He Ming's return and the move decision. The ugly gull was wrapped safely in cloth its owners already had, not because anyone thought it valuable to a buyer but because a friend's bad painting had become theirs. Zhou left it beside the notebook. An said the new room might make it look worse. She answered that the superintendent would interpret this as a challenge. They laughed and locked the door. Across the coast, He Ming traveled home through stages, returning to people whose choices had continued while she was away.
